problem: The dev plugin got a minor bump (4.2.3 → 4.3.0), and so did dev/.codex-plugin/plugin.json. This diff only modifies an existing skill and adds no skill, agent, command or hook. Under the docs/conventions.md 'Plugin Version Bump Rules' table, 'Any shipped asset modified' is a patch bump.
failure: Compare the diff with docs/conventions.md lines 125-131. The only change type that applies is 'Any shipped asset modified | patch', which means 4.2.4, but both manifests show 4.3.0.
fix: Set the version to 4.2.4 in both dev/.claude-plugin/plugin.json and dev/.codex-plugin/plugin.json, and update the CHANGELOG entry to match.

problem: QA_REJECT_RE matches rejection words even when they are negated or zero, so qa-verifier approvals are recorded as qa-reject.
failure: A qa-verifier result like 'PASS — no blocking issues, 0 failed' or 'All criteria met; no P0/P1 findings' matches `blocking`, `failed` or `P0`. The sync path (line 616) and the async path (line 587) then record it as qa-reject, so approvals alone can reach Signal 8's ≥2 threshold.
fix: Count a result as a rejection only when it contains an explicit verdict (e.g. FAIL/REJECT as the verdict token), or exclude results that also contain a PASS verdict.

problem: The async qa-reject path counts any teammate-message, task-notification or agent-message that mentions 'qa-verif' anywhere. It never checks that qa-verifier sent the message.
failure: An implementer message 'done, 2 tests failed earlier, handing to qa-verifier', or a reviewer reporting 'P1: qa-verifier.md frontmatter …', matches both QA_ATTRIB_RE and QA_REJECT_RE. Either one is recorded as a qa-verifier rejection.
fix: Attribute by the message's sender or agent-name field instead of a substring match in the body.

problem: The ci-fail check excludes only `reason: "timeout"`. It still counts ci-wait's ci-status-error verdict, and errored Bash timeouts, as CI failures. That contradicts the taxonomy rule that timeouts are excluded.
failure: When hub/gh fails, ci-wait.sh prints `{"passed":false,"reason":"ci-status returned: error"}`. A Bash tool timeout on ci-wait.sh sets is_error=True and skips the timeout exclusion. Both are recorded as [ci-fail].
fix: Exclude non-verdict reasons such as status errors, and exclude tool-timeout errors, before classifying a result as ci-fail.

problem: The hook-deny check matches the command's own output text. A failing test or CI run whose output mentions a hook name is therefore reclassified as hook-deny.
failure: `python3 dev/hooks/commit-guard/test_guard.py --test` fails and prints 'FAIL — commit-guard …' with is_error set. HOOK_DENY_RE matches it, so a real test failure is reported as [hook-deny] and routed to update-config.
fix: Detect hook denials from the hook-denial envelope or marker in the tool_result, not from arbitrary stdout.

problem: verifier_failures stores only (kind, detail) and drops the session. Signal 8's rules depend on whether failures came from the same session or from different ones.
failure: Three ci-fail entries from one rework loop in a single session look the same as three from separate sessions. The taxonomy's same-session exclusion cannot be applied, and the brief's 'session/kind' citation cannot be filled in.
fix: Include the session id in each verifier_failures entry and in its output line.

problem: VERIFIER_CAP keeps the first 30 entries in file-glob order. Session UUIDs sort randomly, not by time, so recent failures can be dropped.
failure: In a project with 200 ci-fail entries, the output shows 30 arbitrary entries plus '[dropped 170]'. A regression that started after a recent change can fall entirely into the dropped set.
fix: Sort entries by timestamp and keep the most recent ones, the same way PROMPTS does.

problem: CI_COMMAND_RE matches substrings anywhere in a Bash command, so search and read commands that merely mention a test name count as CI runs.
failure: `grep -rn pytest docs/` exits 1 when nothing matches, with is_error set, and is recorded as `[ci-fail] … [matched: pytest]`.
fix: Anchor the match to the executable position of the command, or exclude grep/rg/cat-style commands.

problem: rec_err, the record-level toolUseResult error flag, is applied to every tool_result block in the record, not only the block it belongs to.
failure: In a user record that batches several tool_result blocks with an errored toolUseResult, a passing pytest block inherits is_err=True and is recorded as ci-fail.
fix: Use each block's own is_error, and apply rec_err only when the record contains a single tool_result.

problem: The sync path recognizes qa-verifier only when `subagent_type == "qa-verifier"` exactly, while the async path accepts looser variants. The sync path misses namespaced roles.
failure: In a downstream repo that spawns the role as `dev:qa-verifier`, synchronous rejections are never added to pending_tools and are silently dropped. The same verdict delivered asynchronously is collected.
fix: Use the same QA_ATTRIB_RE-style match for subagent_type on the sync path.
